subject: dsa
title: Validate Binary Search Tree
summary: A node-vs-parent check isn't enough: every node must fall inside the (low, high) range its ancestors imply. Pass the range down — going left tightens the high bound, going right tightens the low bound.
problem: Determine whether a binary tree is a valid binary search tree, where every node is greater than all nodes to its left and less than all to its right.

steps.caption: A valid BST needs every node to fit the (low, high) range set by all its ancestors — not just its parent. Pass a shrinking range down.
Root 5 has range (-inf, +inf). Everything in its left subtree must be < 5, everything in its right subtree > 5.
Left child 3 must be in (-inf, 5). It fits.
Right child 7 must be in (5, +inf). It fits, and now its subtree is bounded to (5, 7) on the left and (7, +inf) on the right.
But 7's left child is 4. Its allowed range is (5, 7), and 4 < 5 — it's on the wrong side of the root, even though 4 < 7 looks fine locally.
A node breaks its inherited range, so this is not a valid BST.
